cars-jdm-legends.question: Which car has the highest horsepower?

results.title: cars-jdm-legends.md — part 2
results.text:
## Nissan Skyline GT-R (R34)
- Years: 1999–2002
- Engine: RB26DETT, 2.6L twin-turbo inline-6
- Horsepower: 276 hp (officially — capped by Japan's "gentlemen's agreement"; real output widely believed higher)
- Torque: 293 lb-ft (392 Nm)
- 0–60 mph: 4.7 s
- Top speed: 156 mph (electronically limited)
- Curb weight: 3,439 lb (V-Spec and Nür trims run heavier)
- Drivetrain: ATTESA E-TS Pro AWD

## Mazda RX-7 (FD3S)
- Years: 1992–2002
- Engine: 13B-REW, 1.3L twin-rotor sequential twin-turbo
- Horsepower: 255 hp (JDM base) — up to 280 hp on the late Spirit R
- Torque: 217 lb-ft
- 0–60 mph: 4.9 s
- Top speed: 155 mph (limited); Spirit R models to 161 mph
- Curb weight: ~2,800 lb
- Note: lightest car in this set, prized for 50/50 weight distribution.

# JDM Legends — Spec Comparison (Dataset 2)

> Verified via web search against published/enthusiast-site specs (August 2026). Where sources disagreed, the most commonly cited figure was used and noted. Treat 0–60 and top-speed figures as representative for the trim listed, not a single official factory number — these vary by market (JDM/US/EU), test methodology, and model year even for the same nameplate.

## Toyota Supra MK4 (A80) Turbo
- Years: 1993–2002
- Engine: 2JZ-GTE, 3.0L twin-turbo inline-6
- Horsepower: 321 hp
- Torque: 315 lb-ft
- 0–60 mph: 4.6 s
- Top speed: 155 mph (electronically limited; unlimited US models observed near 177 mph)
- Curb weight: 3,560 lb

I took the paper from him and read as follows:

“TO THE RED-HEADED LEAGUE: On account of the bequest of the late
Ezekiah Hopkins, of Lebanon, Pennsylvania, U.S.A., there is now another
vacancy open which entitles a member of the League to a salary of £ 4 a
week for purely nominal services. All red-headed men who are sound in
body and mind and above the age of twenty-one years, are eligible.
Apply in person on Monday, at eleven o’clock, to Duncan Ross, at the
offices of the League, 7 Pope’s Court, Fleet Street.”


“What on earth does this mean?” I ejaculated after I had twice read
over the extraordinary announcement.

Holmes chuckled and wriggled in his chair, as was his habit when in
high spirits. “It is a little off the beaten track, isn’t it?” said he.
“And now, Mr. Wilson, off you go at scratch and tell us all about
yourself, your household, and the effect which this advertisement had
upon your fortunes. You will first make a note, Doctor, of the paper
and the date.”
